outlier.evidence: Mild: one point above the other A ratings, but the only rating above 7 among all seven reviews in both committees. Had it been a 7, A's mean would be 6.75, close to B's 6.67. The 8 rests on the longest review (6 h), four questions on capacity, loss design and language modelling, and two follow-up posts. Reviewer_sKB5 rose to 8 after the authors supplied a new capacity table and wrote 'I want to see this paper accepted'. The praise 'very well written' is generous: the same review lists typos on four lines, a broken sentence and a forgotten placeholder.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: The original review is two sentences (a one-line summary and a one-line verdict) with no reference to any section, equation or result, and 'n/a' for limitations. The specific objection (no comparison with TPR, NSCL, Logic Tensor Networks) appeared only in a discussion post on 2021-08-18. The later raise cites 'the enthusiasm of the other reviewers', and the final text still notes 'the lack of comparative evaluation results'.

checkable_claims.claim: A discussion of binding capacity is entirely missing.
checkable_claims.evidence: The authors conceded it ('We will add reference to the capacity results of Plate') and posted a new capacity table. The supplied PDF is the camera-ready; its Section 3.1 now has an added capacity paragraph that points to Appendix D.

checkable_claims.claim: The evaluation compares only standard networks with and without the HRR output layer; there is no comparison with TPR, NSCL, Logic Tensor Networks or similar systems.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 5 baselines are FC, XML-CNN and AttentionXML, each with a fully connected output layer. Section 2 calls first-order-logic systems 'beyond the scope of our current study'.

checkable_claims.claim: The contribution in Section 3.1 is incremental and rather straightforward.
checkable_claims.evidence: Equation 3 divides each Fourier coefficient by its magnitude. Reviewer_rafZ ('simple fix') and Reviewer_uoCQ ('small but important modification') describe it the same way. Whether simple means incremental is a judgment, not a fact.

checkable_claims.claim: Related work omits Plate's own use of HRRs in gradient-based learning systems (his book, chapter 5).
checkable_claims.evidence: The camera-ready still cites only Plate 1995 and still says 'no work to our knowledge has successfully used a VSA of fixed length in gradient based learning'. The authors' reply to Reviewer_rafZ does not answer this point.

checkable_claims.claim: Results are at least in the same ballpark as state-of-the-art methods.
checkable_claims.evidence: True only in part. Table 1 marks three HRR cells within 5% of the published XML-CNN or AttentionXML scores (EURLex-4K, Amazon-13K, Wiki10-31K); these are 2017 and 2019 methods. On Amazon-670K, HRR-FC P@1 is 19.9 against 34.6 for its own FC baseline.

checkable_claims.claim: The choice of HRR dimension d is arbitrary.
checkable_claims.evidence: The authors replied 'The choice of d was fairly arbitrary'. Section 5.3 uses d'=400 or 3000 with no stated rule.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_sKB5 edited 2021-08-18: 'increase my score to an 8'. Reviewer_m8WY edited 2021-08-18: 'I will raise my score to a 7'. Reviewer_LW6b edited 2021-08-23: 'I have increased my score accordingly'; the original text said 'I don't believe that the paper can be accepted'. Reviewer_rafZ never posted and never edited. So A's pre-rebuttal mean was at most 6.25; the final mean is 7.0.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: Reviewer_sKB5 was convinced by answers to the loss-function questions and by a new table: error-free retrieval capacity of projected HRRs reaches 384 pairs at d=8100, while naive HRRs stop at 24. Reviewer_m8WY, unfamiliar with HRRs, cited 'discussion of significance with reviewers rafZ and sKB5'. Reviewer_LW6b cited 'the enthusiasm of the other reviewers' and a second look at the supplement. No comparative evaluation was added, and the final LW6b text says so.

ac.evidence: Spotlight on a 7.0 mean with one 8. The meta-review paraphrases Reviewer_rafZ: 'will likely spark future work' (rafZ: 'will likely spur greater interest') and 'fairly broad interest' (rafZ: 'a fairly diverse audience'). It says the clarifications made 'all reviewers much more confident'; Reviewer_rafZ never took part, and Reviewer_LW6b still notes no comparative evaluation. Its 'very effective' refers to size, which Table 2 supports (output layer 59-99.6% smaller, whole network 5-42% smaller).

main_reasons_for_decision: Mean 7.0 after three of four reviewers raised their scores in discussion
A champion (Reviewer_sKB5, 8) who saw the paper as filling a gap in trainable fixed-size binding
The rebuttal closed the champion's one stated weakness (capacity) with new results
The AC adopted Reviewer_rafZ's significance case: promising, likely to spark future work, broad interest

outlier.evidence: Ratings 7, 6, 7, none above 7. All three reviews share the same reservation about the application.

checkable_claims.claim: Multi-label classification does not use the key feature of HRRs, the ability to represent complex symbolic structure.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 4 binds every label vector to one of two fixed role vectors, p or m (eqs. 4-5). There is no nesting and no other role. The authors agreed: 'more complex hierarchical/nested symbolic mechanics would be stronger'.

checkable_claims.claim: The method uses two fixed orthogonal role vectors, and learning the role and filler vectors has little effect.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 4: m is 'any vector orthogonal to p', and neither changes during training. Section 5.5 and Table 5: fixed and learned label vectors differ by at most 1.56 P@5 points.

checkable_claims.claim: The authors replaced AttentionXML's hierarchical attention head with a fully connected layer.
checkable_claims.evidence: Sections 5 and 5.2 say the hierarchical prediction head 'is replaced with a fully connected layer'.

checkable_claims.claim: Performance is comparable and in some cases SOTA-exceeding.
checkable_claims.evidence: No HRR result in Table 1 exceeds published state of the art. The paper marks only three HRR cells as within 5% of XML-CNN or AttentionXML and states 'State-of-the-art XML performance is not a goal'. HRR beats its own baseline in several cells; that is a different claim. The misread is favourable to the paper and did not raise the rating above 6.

checkable_claims.claim: Table 1 applies different models to different datasets with no explanation.
checkable_claims.evidence: The authors replied 'We will add this explanation to the document'. The camera-ready now explains it in Sections 5 and 5.1 (raw text not available; footnote 3).

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_uoCQ edited 2021-08-21 and posted 'I've decided to increase my rating to 7'. Reviewer_rRrp did not edit; the 2021-08-27 post thanks the authors but says 'we're hindered a bit by not being able to see an actual revision'. Reviewer_M8pZ never posted and never edited. So B's pre-rebuttal mean was at most 6.33; the final mean is 6.67.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: Reviewer_uoCQ accepted the authors' point that the problem solved is making HRRs learnable by backpropagation: 'this work will provide a foundation'. Reviewer_rRrp's concerns were framing and application, which a reply cannot fix, so the rating stayed at 6. In B the authors offered promised text and a worked example, not new results.

ac.evidence: Poster on a 6.67 mean. The meta-review is two sentences. 'Provides a foundation for other systems to build on' repeats Reviewer_uoCQ's update. 'The results are not compelling that such representations will be useful in applications' states the reservation that Reviewer_uoCQ, Reviewer_rRrp and Reviewer_M8pZ all raised.

main_reasons_for_decision: All three reviewers said the XML demonstration does not exercise what HRRs are for
The AC judged the application results not compelling and accepted on technical novelty
Thin discussion: one score raise, one reviewer silent, one unmoved

issues_only_a: No analysis of binding capacity versus dimension (Reviewer_sKB5, Reviewer_rafZ)
No comparison with other neuro-symbolic systems such as TPR, NSCL or Logic Tensor Networks (Reviewer_LW6b)
Novelty claim ignores Plate's own gradient-based use of HRRs (Reviewer_rafZ)
No theory for why the projection improves retrieval, and no case for HRR over other VSAs (Reviewer_rafZ)
Alternative exponential loss and objective forms (Reviewer_sKB5)
issues_only_b: XML binds labels to only two fixed roles, so compositional binding is never tested (Reviewer_uoCQ, Reviewer_M8pZ, Reviewer_rRrp)
Unclear purpose: what problem the method solves and what it would replace (Reviewer_uoCQ, Reviewer_rRrp)
AttentionXML's head replaced by a fully connected layer; no comparison with attention, hashing or distillation output layers (Reviewer_rRrp)
Table 1 applies different models to different datasets without explanation (Reviewer_uoCQ)
shared_issues: The HRR background in Section 3 is hard for non-experts (Reviewer_m8WY, Reviewer_LW6b; Reviewer_rRrp, Reviewer_uoCQ)
Tensor Product Representation work is missing from related work (Reviewer_sKB5, Reviewer_LW6b; Reviewer_M8pZ)
The projection step is a small, simple change (Reviewer_rafZ, Reviewer_LW6b; Reviewer_uoCQ)
Not state of the art on XML, and only one task (Reviewer_m8WY, Reviewer_rafZ; Reviewer_uoCQ, Reviewer_rRrp, Reviewer_M8pZ)
Many typos and an 'XXX lines of code' placeholder (Reviewer_sKB5, Reviewer_m8WY, Reviewer_rafZ; Reviewer_uoCQ, Reviewer_rRrp)
verdict: Both committees saw the same facts; A's discussion lifted its scores to a spotlight, while B's reviewers kept their doubt about the XML demonstration. Every reviewer describes the same contribution: a projection step that makes HRRs trainable, shown on XML with large output-layer compression and accuracy near the baselines except at 670K labels. Before the discussion A's mean was at most 6.25, below B's final 6.67; three raises in discussion carried A to 7.0. In A, Reviewer_sKB5 received a new capacity table and rose to 8, asking for acceptance. Reviewer_m8WY and Reviewer_LW6b then raised their scores, each citing the other reviewers' views. A's AC repeated Reviewer_rafZ's case for broad interest and future work. In B, all three reviewers said that XML, with two fixed roles, never tests what HRRs are for. Only Reviewer_uoCQ moved, to 7. B's AC wrote that the results do not show usefulness in applications. A weighted the enabling step; B weighted the thin demonstration.
candidate_reasons: Score raises by deference to peers
New results shown only to A
evidence_pointers: Authors' 'Reply^2' to Reviewer_sKB5 with the capacity table (Committee A)
